POST /api/admin/practitioners/{id}/refresh with X-Tenant-Id: mayo-mayo returned 200 {"outcome":"REFRESHED",...,"name":"Reyes, Aurelia B, MD","epicUserId":"PERID-NONAME-001","epicProviderId":"PROVID-9001","role":"Anesthesiologist","email":"aurelia.reyes@example.org"}. The app log shows the lookup was the direct identifier search, not a name search: 'MayoGetPractitionerR4Command : Invoking url: .../Practitioner?identifier=urn%3Aoid%3A...737384.135%7CPERID-NONAME-001'. evidence.negative: Three inverse cases, all observed on the running app. (1) NO_MATCH is not an error: mayo-mayo practitioner 1111...1112 ('PERID-NAMED-002', a PERID the stub Epic has no Practitioner for) returned 200 {"outcome":"NO_MATCH"} and the attempt was recorded - last_refreshed_at went from NULL to 2026-08-24 19:03:34 - and the UI row button rendered btn-outline-secondary '–' with title 'FHIR has no practitioner for this id (e.g. a service account)'. (2) A real Epic failure is distinguishable: I killed the stub Epic and re-refreshed the SAME practitioner that had just returned 200 REFRESHED; it returned 502 {"outcome":"FAILED"} and still stamped last_refreshed_at (19:05:33), the documented tradeoff. MGB against its unreachable stage Epic likewise returned 502 FAILED. (3) The capability gate is real, not cosmetic: demo-demo (no FHIR integration) returned 200 {"refreshSupported":false} and in the UI the Practitioners tab for demo-demo showed no bulk button and no refresh column, while demo bulk refresh returned {"refreshed":0,"noMatch":0,"skipped":1,"failed":0}. MGB regression checks passed unchanged: a practitioner with a linked user hit MGBGetPractitionerR4Command 'Practitioner?identifier=...|loopuser' (clientUserId path), a named practitioner with no linked user hit 'Practitioner?name=Mary+Jones' (name search), and a nameless one short-circuited with 'No name to search practitioners by for epic user id: MGBUSER-NONAME' and never queried Epic. Bulk of 201 ids returned 400 'Refresh at most 200 practitioners per request (got 201)'.

jira_comment:
I validated this against a throwaway instance built from main (e7eeafd6c), exercising both the API and the real admin UI.

Positive: a mayo-mayo practitioner with a PERID and no name refreshed successfully. The log shows the direct identifier lookup (Practitioner?identifier=<person-id-system>|PERID-NONAME-001), not a name search, and the row came back with name, PROVID, role and email filled in and last_refreshed_at stamped. In the UI the Practitioners tab for mayo-mayo rendered the refresh controls off the new capabilities endpoint, the row button turned green with a check, and bulk reported "1 refreshed, 1 no match, 0 skipped, 0 failed".

Negative: a PERID with no Practitioner behind it returned 200 with outcome NO_MATCH and still recorded the attempt, while the same practitioner with Epic unreachable returned 502 FAILED - so a clean miss and an outage are now distinguishable. demo-demo reported refreshSupported=false and showed no refresh controls at all. MGB was unchanged: linked users still resolve by clientUserId, named practitioners still go through the name search, and a nameless one short-circuits without querying Epic. A bulk of 201 ids was rejected with 400.

Red check: I compiled the pre-fix PractitionerService and PractitionerAdminController from the parent commit, swapped them into the running container and restarted. Capabilities 404'd and the nameless Mayo PERID failed with 400 "Cannot refresh practitioner: needs either a clientUserId or both epicUserId and name" - the exact gate this ticket removes - and the unmatched PERID returned the same 400 as an outage would. I restored the shipped classes, verified the checksums matched, and re-ran the positive green.

One caveat: this instance has no Mayo OAuth keys, so Epic was a local stub answering the exact request shape and Bundle totals the Mayo command builds. The outcome mapping is fully exercised; real Mayo Epic content is not.

Automation: the backend unit tests that shipped with this already cover the outcomes, the bulk tallies, the 200-id cap and both capabilities answers, so I would not duplicate them. The gap is the frontend, which has no unit runner yet, so I plan qa-suite supplemental tests for the capability-driven controls appearing for an integrated tenant and staying hidden for a non-integrated one, plus API-level checks for the 200-NO_MATCH vs 502-FAILED split and the bulk size cap.
